The Mosquito Detection Sensor project is designed to identify the presence of mosquitoes in an environment using a combination of electronic sensors, signal processing techniques, and machine learning classification. The purpose of this project is to provide an early-warning system to help reduce mosquito-borne diseases by detecting mosquitoes before they become a major threat.
Mic sensor (sound sensor for mosquito wing sound)
1.ESP8266 (NodeMCU)Acts as the main controller or “brain” of the project.Receives data from all sensors, processes it.
2.Mic SensorSenses low‑frequency sound produced by mosquito wings.Detects surrounding sounds, filters noise, and identifies mosquito
4.OLED Display (Mini)Placed on the breadboard and connected to NodeMCU.Displays humidity and temperature values from DHT11.

This mosquito detection sensor project successfully demonstrates how to integrate sound sensing, humidity monitoring, and microcontroller-based data processing to detect and indicate the presence of mosquitoes in a targeted area.

By using components such as the ESP8266 NodeMCU, DHT11 humidity sensor, OLED display, and basic connecting hardware, the system is able to sense environmental conditions, filter sound signals, and provide accurate, real-time feedback.

The approach not only helps in identifying mosquito density but also showcases the practical application of IoT for environmental monitoring, with the potential to enhance public health and safety through early detection and preventive action .
